title.en: Volume 59 Biographies 24: Three Sons of Emperor Yang

sentences.zh: 元德太子元德太子昭，煬帝長子也，生而高祖命養宮中。

translations.literal: The Yuande Heir Apparent Zhao—the Yuande Heir Apparent—was Emperor Yang's eldest son; from birth the High Ancestor ordered that he be reared in the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Zhao, posthumously honored as the Yuande Heir Apparent, was Emperor Yang's eldest son. From birth Emperor Wen ordered that he be raised in the palace.

sentences.zh: 三歲時，於玄武門弄石師子，高祖與文獻後至其所。

translations.literal: When he was three, he was playing with a stone lion at the Xuanwu Gate; the High Ancestor and Empress Wenxian came to where he was.
translations.idiomatic: At the age of three he was playing with a stone lion at the Xuanwu Gate when Emperor Wen and Empress Wenxian came to where he was.

sentences.zh: 高祖適患腰痛，舉手憑後，昭因避去，如此者再三。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor happened to be suffering from back pain and raised his hand to lean on the empress; Zhao thereupon withdrew—this happened three times.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen happened to be troubled by back pain and raised his hand to lean on the empress; each time Zhao drew aside out of propriety, and this happened three times.

sentences.zh: 高祖歎曰：「天生長者，誰複教乎！

translations.literal: The High Ancestor sighed and said: "Born a man of thorough propriety—who else could teach him!"
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen sighed and said, "He is born a man of thorough propriety—who could teach him such conduct!"

sentences.zh: 」由是大奇之。

translations.literal: " Because of this he greatly marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: " From this he came to regard the boy with wonder.

sentences.zh: 高祖嘗謂曰：「當為爾娶婦。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor once said to him: "When the time comes I shall find you a wife."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once told him, "When the time comes I shall find you a wife."

sentences.zh: 」昭應聲而泣。

translations.literal: " Zhao answered with a cry.
translations.idiomatic: " Zhao burst into tears at once.

sentences.zh: 高祖問其故，對曰：「漢王未婚時，恆在至尊所，一朝娶婦，便則出外。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor asked the reason; he replied: "When the Prince of Han was still unmarried, he was always at Your Majesty's side; once he took a wife, he went outside at once.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen asked why; he answered, "When Prince Guang was still unmarried he was always at Your Majesty's side; the day he married he went out to his own residence at once.

sentences.zh: 懼將違離，是以啼耳。

translations.literal: I fear I shall be parted from you, and that is why I weep."
translations.idiomatic: I am afraid I shall be separated from you—that is why I weep."

sentences.zh: 」上歎其有至性，特鍾愛焉。

translations.literal: " The sovereign sighed at his utmost sincerity and lavished special affection on him.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor marveled at his deep filial nature and favored him with special affection.

sentences.zh: 年十二，立為河南王。

translations.literal: At the age of twelve he was invested as King of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: When he was twelve he was made King of Henan.

sentences.zh: 仁壽初，徙為晉王，拜內史令，兼左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Renshou era he was transferred to Prince of Jin, appointed Director of the Palace Secretariat, and concurrently General-in-Chief of the Left Guards.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Renshou era he was moved to Prince of Jin, named Director of the Palace Secretariat, and concurrently made General-in-Chief of the Left Guards.

sentences.zh: 後三年，轉雍州牧。

translations.literal: Three years later he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province.
translations.idiomatic: Three years after that he was appointed Governor of Yong Province.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，便幸洛陽宮，昭留守京師。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he went at once to the Luoyang palace; Zhao remained to hold the capital.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang acceded, he went at once to the Luoyang palace while Zhao stayed behind to guard the capital.

sentences.zh: ，帝遣使者立為皇太子。

translations.literal: The emperor sent envoys to invest him as crown prince.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then sent envoys to invest him as crown prince.

sentences.zh: 昭有武力，能引強弩。

translations.literal: Zhao had physical strength and could draw powerful crossbows.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao was physically strong and could draw powerful crossbows.

sentences.zh: 性謙沖，言色恂恂，未嘗忿怒。

translations.literal: By nature he was humble and restrained; his speech and bearing were mild and respectful, and he was never angry.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was modest and self-effacing; in speech and countenance he was gentle and deferential, and he was never seen angry.

sentences.zh: 有深嫌可責者，但雲「大不是」。

translations.literal: When someone had done something seriously blameworthy, he would only say, "That is very wrong."
translations.idiomatic: Even when someone had given grave cause for blame, he would only say, "That is quite wrong."

sentences.zh: 所膳不許多品，帷席極於儉素。

translations.literal: His meals were not allowed many courses; curtains and mats were extremely plain.
translations.idiomatic: His table was not served many dishes, and his curtains and mats were kept severely plain.

sentences.zh: 臣吏有老父母者，必親問其安否，歲時皆有惠賜。

translations.literal: If among his subordinates there were those with aged parents, he would personally inquire after their well-being, and at year's end always bestowed favors.
translations.idiomatic: When any of his officials had elderly parents, he would personally ask after their health, and at the turn of each year he always gave them gifts.

sentences.zh: 其仁愛如此。

translations.literal: Such was his benevolence.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the kindness he showed.

sentences.zh: 明年，朝於洛陽。

translations.literal: The next year he attended court at Luoyang.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he came to court at Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 後數月，將還京師，願得少留，帝不許，拜請無數。

translations.literal: Some months later, as he was about to return to the capital, he begged to remain a little longer; the emperor would not allow it, and though he bowed and pleaded countless times—
translations.idiomatic: Some months later, when he was about to return to the capital, he asked to stay a little longer; the emperor refused, and he bowed and pleaded again and again without success.

sentences.zh: 體素肥，因致勞疾。

translations.literal: His constitution was naturally stout, and thereby he fell ill from exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: His body was naturally heavy, and from this he fell ill with exhaustion.

sentences.zh: 帝令巫者視之，雲：「房陵王為祟。

translations.literal: The emperor had a shaman examine him; the man said: "The Prince of Fangling is afflicting him."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had a shaman look into the matter; the man said, "Prince Yong of Fangling is haunting him."

sentences.zh: 」未幾而薨。

translations.literal: " Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: " Before long he died.

sentences.zh: 詔內史侍郎虞世基為哀冊文曰：

translations.literal: An edict ordered Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Yu Shiji to compose a lamentation for the funerary book, which read:
translations.idiomatic: An edict directed Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat Yu Shiji to compose the lamentation text for the funerary book. It read:

sentences.zh: :維七月癸丑朔二十三日，皇太子薨于行宮。

translations.literal: On the twenty-third day of the first month of the seventh month, the cyclical day guichou, the crown prince died at the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, on the first day of the guichou cycle, the crown prince died at the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 粵三年五月庚辰朔六日，將遷座于莊陵，禮也。

translations.literal: On the sixth day of the first month of the fifth month in the third year, cyclical day gengchen, the coffin will be moved to Zhuang Mausoleum—such is the rite.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixth day of the fifth month in the third year of his reign, on the gengchen cycle, the coffin is to be transferred to Zhuang Mausoleum, as ritual requires.

sentences.zh: 蜃綍宵載，鶴關曉辟，肅文物以具陳，儼賓從其如昔。

translations.literal: The imperial carriage is borne by night; at dawn the Crane Gate opens; ritual objects are solemnly arrayed in full; the entourage stands in ordered ranks as of old.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial hearse moves by night; at dawn the palace gate opens; ritual regalia is set out in full solemn array, and the retinue stands in ranks as before.

sentences.zh: 皇帝悼離方之雲晦，嗟震宮之虧象，顧守器以長懷，臨登餕而興想。

translations.literal: The emperor grieves that the clouds over the departing quarter have darkened, laments the diminished image of the Thunder Palace, looks long upon the heir who guarded the vessel, and, facing the ascending offerings, is moved to thought.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourns the darkened clouds over the land of the departed, laments the broken image of the eastern palace, broods long over the heir who held the vessel of state, and, as the funeral offerings are raised, is stirred to grief.

sentences.zh: 先遠戒日，占謀允從，庭彝徹祖，階所收重，抗銘旌以啟路，動徐輪于振容。

translations.literal: The day forewarned by the departed is observed; divination and counsel are followed; ancestral vessels are displayed in the hall; the steps receive the honored bier; inscribed banners are raised to open the way; the slow wheels move upon the mourning carriage.
translations.idiomatic: The day appointed for the departed is kept; augury and counsel agree; ancestral vessels are set out in the hall; the bier is received upon the steps; inscribed banners are raised to clear the road, and the wheels of the mourning carriage turn slowly onward.

sentences.zh: 揆行度名，累德彰諡，爰詔史冊，式遵典志，俾浚哲之徽猷，播長久乎天地。

translations.literal: We measure conduct to fix the name, accumulate virtue to display the posthumous title; thus we charge the historical records, following the canonical statutes, that his far-reaching wisdom and fine conduct may be broadcast long upon heaven and earth.
translations.idiomatic: His deeds are weighed to fix his name, his accumulated virtue to proclaim his posthumous title; the annals are charged, following canonical precedent, that his luminous wisdom and merit may resound through heaven and earth for ages to come.

sentences.zh: 其辭曰：

translations.literal: The text reads:
translations.idiomatic: The text reads:

sentences.zh: :宸基峻極，帝緒會昌。

translations.literal: The imperial foundation rises to its utmost height; the imperial line meets its flourishing age.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial foundation towers to its height; the royal line enters its age of glory.

sentences.zh: 體元襲聖，儀耀重光。

translations.literal: Embodying the Origin, inheriting the Sage; his bearing shines with renewed radiance.
translations.idiomatic: He embodied the primal virtue and inherited the sage's mantle; his presence shone with redoubled brilliance.

sentences.zh: 氣秀春陸，神華少陽。

translations.literal: His vital breath flourished like spring upon the land; his spirit blossomed in the eastern quarter of youth.
translations.idiomatic: His vital spirit flourished like spring upon the earth; his brilliance shone in the quarter of youth.

sentences.zh: 居周軼誦，處漢韜莊。

translations.literal: In Zhou he surpassed the recitations; in Han he concealed his solemnity.
translations.idiomatic: Among the sons of Zhou he surpassed the classic recitations; among the princes of Han he bore himself with hidden gravity.

sentences.zh: 有縱生知，誕膺惟睿。

translations.literal: He possessed innate knowledge from birth and received the sole charge of wisdom.
translations.idiomatic: Knowledge came to him from birth; he was endowed alone with sagely wisdom.

sentences.zh: 性道觿日，幾深綺歲。

translations.literal: His nature and the Way showed from the day of his girdling; subtle insight came in his brocade years.
translations.idiomatic: His nature and the Way appeared from the day he was girded; subtle understanding came in the flower of youth.

sentences.zh: 降跡大成，俯情多藝。

translations.literal: He descended to trace the Great Completion and bent his heart to many arts.
translations.idiomatic: He took his place in the great completion of learning and bent his heart to many accomplishments.

sentences.zh: 樹親建國，命懿作籓。

translations.literal: He planted kin and founded states, appointing the virtuous to serve as feudatories.
translations.idiomatic: He was enfeoffed among the royal kin and founded his state, charged with virtue to rule as a prince.

sentences.zh: 威蕤先路，舄奕渠門。

translations.literal: His majesty adorned the vanguard; his splendor filled the palace gates.
translations.idiomatic: His majesty went before on the road; his splendor filled the palace gates.

sentences.zh: 庸服有紀，分器惟尊。

translations.literal: His service had its proper measure; in the division of vessels he held the highest rank.
translations.idiomatic: His duties were ordered by rule; in the apportionment of regalia he held the highest place.

sentences.zh: 風高楚殿，雅盛梁園。

translations.literal: His refinement towered like the Chu hall; his elegance flourished like the Liang garden.
translations.idiomatic: His refinement rose like the halls of Chu; his literary grace flourished like the gardens of Liang.

sentences.zh: 睿後膺儲，天人協順。

translations.literal: The wise heir received the succession; heaven and man were in accord.
translations.idiomatic: The sagely heir received the succession; heaven and mankind were in harmony.

sentences.zh: 本茂條遠，基崇體峻。

translations.literal: His root was luxuriant and his branches far-reaching; his foundation was lofty and his stature towering.
translations.idiomatic: His root was deep and his branches far-reaching; his foundation was high and his stature imposing.

sentences.zh: 改王參墟，奄有唐、晉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to prince at Canxu and came to hold Tang and Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He was made prince at the ancient seat of Canxu and came to hold the domains of Tang and Jin.

sentences.zh: 在貴能謙，居沖益慎。

translations.literal: Though noble he could be humble; dwelling in modesty he grew ever more cautious.
translations.idiomatic: Though exalted in rank he remained humble; dwelling in modesty he grew ever more careful.

sentences.zh: 封畿千里，閶闔九重。

translations.literal: His fief stretched a thousand li; the palace gates rose ninefold.
translations.idiomatic: His domain stretched a thousand li; the palace gates towered in ninefold depth.

sentences.zh: 神州王化，禁旅軍容。

translations.literal: He bore the kingly transformation of the divine land and the military bearing of the palace guard.
translations.idiomatic: He bore the royal civilizing charge of the central realm and the martial array of the palace guards.

sentences.zh: 瞻言偃草，高視折衝。

translations.literal: His words made the grass lie down; his lofty gaze broke the enemy's charge.
translations.idiomatic: His words could still contention like wind over grass; his lofty gaze could break the enemy's charge.

sentences.zh: 帷扆清秘，親賢允屬。

translations.literal: At the screen and armrest he was pure and secretive; to be near the worthy was truly his charge.
translations.idiomatic: At the imperial screen he served in pure confidence; drawing near the worthy was truly his appointed role.

sentences.zh: 泛景風瀾，飛華螭玉。

translations.literal: He floated upon luminous scenes and wind-swept waves; flowering brilliance flew upon dragon and jade.
translations.idiomatic: He moved through scenes of light and wind-swept grandeur; flowering brilliance adorned dragon motifs and jade.

sentences.zh: 揮翰泉湧，敷言藻縟。

translations.literal: When he wielded the brush words gushed like a spring; his spread discourse was brocaded and rich.
translations.idiomatic: When he took up the brush words poured forth like a spring; his discourse was woven with rich ornament.

sentences.zh: 式是便煩，思謀啟沃。

translations.literal: Thus he took on pressing affairs and offered counsel to nourish the ruler.
translations.idiomatic: Thus he took on the weight of affairs and offered counsel to nourish the throne.

sentences.zh: 洪惟積德，豐衍繁祉。

translations.literal: Greatly did he accumulate virtue; blessings spread abroad in abundance.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly did he accumulate virtue; blessings multiplied and flourished.

sentences.zh: 粵自天孫，光升元子。

translations.literal: From the Heaven-descended scion his radiance rose to the eldest son.
translations.idiomatic: From the heaven-descended lineage his light rose to the eldest son.

sentences.zh: 綠車逮事，翠纓奉祀。

translations.literal: In the green carriage he attended to affairs; with the azure tassel he performed the sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: In the green carriage he attended to his duties; with the azure cap-tassel he performed the sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 肅穆滿容，儀形讓齒。

translations.literal: Solemn reverence filled his countenance; in bearing and form he yielded by precedence.
translations.idiomatic: Solemn dignity filled his bearing; in deportment he yielded by rank and age.

sentences.zh: 禮樂交暢，愛敬兼資。

translations.literal: Rites and music flowed together; love and reverence were joined in him.
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music harmonized in him; love and reverence were joined in equal measure.

sentences.zh: 優遊養德，恭己承儀。

translations.literal: At ease he nourished virtue; with reverent self he upheld the rites.
translations.idiomatic: At leisure he cultivated virtue; with reverent bearing he upheld ritual propriety.

sentences.zh: 南山聘隱，東序尊師。

translations.literal: Like the southern mountain he sought the recluse; in the eastern school he honored his teachers.
translations.idiomatic: Like the southern mountain he sought out the hidden worthy; in the eastern school he honored his teachers.

sentences.zh: 有粹神儀，深穆其度。

translations.literal: He possessed pure spiritual bearing; profound and solemn was his measure.
translations.idiomatic: He possessed a pure and spirited bearing; profound and solemn was his demeanor.

sentences.zh: 顯顯觀德，溫溫審諭。

translations.literal: Brightly he displayed virtue for all to see; gently and warmly he instructed.
translations.idiomatic: Brightly he displayed his virtue for all to see; gently and warmly he taught and advised.

sentences.zh: 炯戒齊箴，留連王賦。

translations.literal: Bright was his admonition and equal his caution; lingering was his princely composition.
translations.idiomatic: Bright was his admonition and even his restraint; lingering was his princely literary work.

sentences.zh: 入監出撫，日就月將。

translations.literal: Entering to oversee, going forth to comfort—day by day he advanced, month by month he grew.
translations.idiomatic: Entering the palace to oversee affairs, going forth to comfort the people—day by day he advanced, month by month he matured.

sentences.zh: 沖情玉裕，令問金相。

translations.literal: His modest heart was jade-abundant; his fine reputation had the luster of gold.
translations.idiomatic: His modest heart was rich as jade; his fine reputation shone like gold.

sentences.zh: 宜綏景福，永作元良。

translations.literal: He should have soothed bright blessings and forever served as the eldest worthy.
translations.idiomatic: He should have secured bright blessings and forever stood as the foremost heir.

sentences.zh: 神理冥漠，天道難究。

translations.literal: The divine principle is dark and remote; the way of heaven is hard to fathom.
translations.idiomatic: The divine principle lies dark and remote; the way of heaven is beyond full understanding.

sentences.zh: 仁不必壽，善或愆祐。

translations.literal: Benevolence does not guarantee long life; goodness may miss its blessing.
translations.idiomatic: Benevolence does not assure long life; goodness may yet be denied its blessing.

sentences.zh: 遽瑤山之頹壞，忽桂宮之毀構。

translations.literal: Suddenly the jade mountain collapsed; abruptly the cassia palace's structure was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Suddenly the jade mountain fell in ruin; in an instant the cassia palace's structure was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 痛結幽明，悲纏宇宙。

translations.literal: Grief bound the hidden and the manifest; sorrow entwined the cosmos.
translations.idiomatic: Grief bound the realms of the living and the dead; sorrow filled the universe.

sentences.zh: 慟皇情之深憫，摧具僚其如疚。

translations.literal: The emperor's heart was stricken with deep compassion; all his officials were crushed as if guilty.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's heart was stricken with deep grief; all his officials were crushed as though bearing guilt themselves.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 回環氣朔，荏苒居諸。

translations.literal: The seasons wheel through their cycles; time slips swiftly onward.
translations.idiomatic: The seasons wheel through their cycles; time slips swiftly onward.

sentences.zh: 沾零露於瑤圍，下申霜於玉除。

translations.literal: Scattered dew falls upon the jade enclosure; descending frost settles on the jade steps.
translations.idiomatic: Scattered dew falls upon the jade courtyard; descending frost settles on the jade-paved steps.

sentences.zh: 夜漏盡兮空階曙，曉月懸兮帷殿虛。

translations.literal: The night water-clock runs out and dawn light fills the empty steps; the morning moon hangs and the curtained hall stands void.
translations.idiomatic: The night water-clock runs out and dawn light fills the empty steps; the morning moon hangs while the curtained hall stands empty.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 將寧甫竁，長違望苑。

translations.literal: He is about to find rest in the new tomb and part forever from the Prospect Garden.
translations.idiomatic: He is about to find rest in the new tomb and part forever from the Prospect Garden.

sentences.zh: 渡渭涘於造舟，遵長平之修阪。

translations.literal: They cross the Wei shore by the ferry of Zao; they follow the long slope of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: They cross the Wei shore by the royal ferry and follow the long ascent of Changping.

sentences.zh: 望鶴駕而不追，顧龍樓而日遠。

translations.literal: They gaze upon the crane carriage but cannot pursue; they look back at the dragon tower growing daily more remote.
translations.idiomatic: They gaze upon the imperial hearse but cannot follow; they look back at the dragon tower growing more distant by the day.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 永隔存沒，長分古今。

translations.literal: Forever parted are the living and the dead; long divided are present and past.
translations.idiomatic: Forever parted are the living and the dead; long divided are the present and what has passed.

sentences.zh: 去榮華于人世，即潛之幽深。

translations.literal: He leaves splendor in the human world and enters the hidden depths.
translations.idiomatic: He leaves splendor in the world of the living and enters the hidden depths below.

sentences.zh: 霏夕煙而稍起，慘落景而將沉。

translations.literal: Evening mist rises thinly; the mournful setting sun is about to sink.
translations.idiomatic: Evening mist rises thinly; the mournful setting sun is about to sink.

sentences.zh: 聽哀挽之悽楚，雜灌木之悲吟。

translations.literal: They hear the mournful lament of the funeral dirge, mingled with the sorrowful cry of the thickets.
translations.idiomatic: They hear the mournful dirge of the funeral procession, mingled with the sorrowful sighing of the thickets.

sentences.zh: 紛徒禦而流袂，欷纓弁以沾衿。

translations.literal: The crowd of attendants streams with flowing sleeves; officials in caps sob and wet their collars.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants stream forward with sleeves awash in tears; officials in caps sob and soak their collars.

sentences.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！

translations.literal: Alas, how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: Alas, how mournful!

sentences.zh: 九地黃泉，千年白日。

translations.literal: The ninefold earth and the yellow springs; a thousand years of white sun.
translations.idiomatic: The ninefold earth and the yellow springs; a thousand years of daylight.

sentences.zh: 雖金石之能久，終天壤乎長畢。

translations.literal: Though metal and stone may endure long, in the end heaven and earth reach their long close.
translations.idiomatic: Though metal and stone may endure, in the end heaven and earth themselves reach their close.

sentences.zh: 敢圖芳於篆素，永飛聲而騰實。

translations.literal: We dare inscribe his fragrance upon the red silk, that his fame may fly forever and his merit rise on high.
translations.idiomatic: We dare inscribe his virtue upon the written record, that his fame may soar forever and his merit rise on high.

sentences.zh: 帝深追悼。

translations.literal: The emperor mourned him deeply.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor mourned him with deep grief.

sentences.zh: 有子三人，韋妃生恭皇帝，大劉良娣生燕王倓，小劉良娣生越王侗。

translations.literal: He had three sons: the Consort Wei bore Emperor Gong; the elder Lady Liu, Worthy Companion, bore Prince of Yan Tan; the younger Lady Liu, Worthy Companion, bore Prince of Yue Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Consort Wei bore the future Emperor Gong; the elder Worthy Companion Lady Liu bore Prince Tan of Yan; the younger Worthy Companion Lady Liu bore Prince Tong of Yue.

sentences.zh: 燕王燕王倓字仁安。

translations.literal: Prince of Yan Tan, styled Ren'an—the text repeats the title—
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tan of Yan, whose style name was Ren'an,

sentences.zh: 敏慧美姿儀，煬帝于諸孫中特所鍾愛，常置左右。

translations.literal: was clever and handsome in bearing; among all his grandsons Emperor Yang especially cherished him and kept him constantly at his side.
translations.idiomatic: was clever and handsome in bearing. Among all his grandsons Emperor Yang favored him above the rest and kept him constantly at his side.

sentences.zh: 性好讀書，尤重儒素，非造次所及，有若成人。

translations.literal: By nature he loved reading and especially valued Confucian plainness; what he achieved was not the work of a moment—he was like a grown man.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he loved books and especially honored Confucian simplicity; his attainments were not hurried or shallow—he seemed already a grown man.

sentences.zh: 良娣早終，每至忌日，末嘗不流涕嗚咽。

translations.literal: His Worthy Companion mother died early; on every anniversary of her death he never failed to shed tears and sob.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, a Worthy Companion, had died young; on every anniversary of her death he wept and sobbed without fail.

sentences.zh: 帝由是益以奇之。

translations.literal: Because of this the emperor regarded him with still greater wonder.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this the emperor came to regard him with still greater wonder.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆之際，倓覺變，欲入奏，恐露其事，因與梁公蕭钜、千牛宇文皛等穿芳林門側水竇而入。

translations.literal: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide Tan perceived the uprising; he wished to enter and report but feared exposing the matter, and so with Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Palace Attendant Yuwen Hao, and others he passed through the water conduit beside the Fanglin Gate to enter.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji carried out his regicide, Tan sensed the uprising. He wished to go in and report to the emperor but feared betraying his purpose, so with Duke of Liang Xiao Ju, Palace Attendant Yuwen Hao, and others he entered through the water sluice beside the Fanglin Gate.

sentences.zh: 至玄武門，詭奏曰：「臣卒中惡，命縣俄頃，請得面辭，死無所恨。

translations.literal: At the Xuanwu Gate he made a false report, saying: "Your servant has been stricken with sudden illness; my life hangs by a moment. I beg to take leave of you in person—then I shall die without regret."
translations.idiomatic: At the Xuanwu Gate he sent in a false report: "I have been stricken with sudden illness and my life hangs by a moment. I beg to take leave of Your Majesty in person—then I shall die without regret."

sentences.zh: 」冀以見帝，為司宮者所遏，竟不得聞。

translations.literal: " He hoped thereby to see the emperor, but was blocked by the palace attendants and in the end could not be heard.
translations.idiomatic: " He hoped in this way to reach the emperor, but the palace attendants stopped him, and in the end his message never reached the throne.

sentences.zh: 俄而難作，為賊所害，時年十六。

translations.literal: Before long the catastrophe broke out and he was killed by the rebels; he was sixteen years old.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the uprising erupted and he was killed by the rebels. He was sixteen.

sentences.zh: 越王越王侗字仁謹，美姿儀，性寬厚。

translations.literal: Prince of Yue Tong, styled Renjin—the text repeats the title—was handsome in bearing and generous by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Tong of Yue, whose style name was Renjin, was handsome in bearing and generous by nature.

sentences.zh: ，立為越王。

translations.literal: He was invested as Prince of Yue.
translations.idiomatic: He was invested as Prince of Yue.

sentences.zh: 帝每巡幸，侗常留守東都。

translations.literal: Whenever the emperor went on tour, Tong regularly remained to hold the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the emperor traveled on tour, Tong was regularly left behind to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感作亂之際，與民部尚書樊子蓋拒之。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rose in rebellion, he joined with Minister of the Household Fan Zigai to resist him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he joined Minister of the Household Fan Zigai in resisting him.

sentences.zh: 及玄感平，朝于高陽，拜高陽太守。

translations.literal: When Xuangan was pacified, he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Administrator of Gaoyang.
translations.idiomatic: After Xuangan was defeated, he attended court at Gaoyang and was appointed Administrator of Gaoyang.

sentences.zh: 俄以本官複留守東都。

translations.literal: Before long, in his former capacity, he again remained to hold the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he resumed his former role and was again left to guard the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 十三年，帝幸江都，複令侗與金紫光祿大夫段達、太府卿元文都、攝民部尚書韋津、右武衛將軍皇甫無逸等總留台事。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again charged Tong, together with Grand Master for Splendid Happiness Duan Da, Grand Steward Yuan Wendu, Acting Minister of the Household Wei Jin, General of the Right Martial Guards Huangfu Wuyi, and others, to oversee all affairs of the capital left behind.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the emperor went to Jiangdu and again entrusted Tong, together with Duan Da, Yuan Wendu, Wei Jin acting as Minister of the Household, Huangfu Wuyi as General of the Right Martial Guards, and others, with overall charge of the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及之弑逆也，文都等議，以侗元德太子之子，屬最為近，於是乃共尊立，大赦，改元曰皇泰。

translations.literal: At the time of Yuwen Huaji's regicide, Wendu and the others deliberated; because Tong was a son of the Yuande Heir Apparent and the closest in the imperial line, they thereupon jointly raised him to the throne, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji carried out his regicide, Wendu and the others reasoned that Tong, as a son of the Yuande Heir Apparent, was closest in the imperial line. They jointly enthroned him, proclaimed a general amnesty, and changed the era name to Huangtai.

sentences.zh: 諡帝曰明，廟號世祖。

translations.literal: They gave the deceased emperor the posthumous title Ming and the temple name Shizu.
translations.idiomatic: They gave the murdered emperor the posthumous title Ming and the temple name Shizu.

sentences.zh: 追尊元德太子為孝成皇帝，廟號世宗。

translations.literal: They posthumously honored the Yuande Heir Apparent as Emperor Xiaocheng with the temple name Shizong.
translations.idiomatic: They posthumously honored the Yuande Heir Apparent as Emperor Xiaocheng with the temple name Shizong.

sentences.zh: 尊其母劉良娣為皇太后。

translations.literal: They honored his mother, the Worthy Companion Lady Liu, as Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: They honored his mother, Worthy Companion Lady Liu, as Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 以段達為納言、右翊衛大將軍、攝禮部尚書，王世充亦納言、左翊衛大將軍、攝吏部尚書，元文都內史令、左驍衛大將軍，盧楚亦內史令，皇甫無逸兵部尚書、右武衛大將軍，郭文懿內史侍郎，趙長文黃門侍郎，委以機務，為金書鐵券，藏之宮掖。

translations.literal: Duan Da was made Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guards, and Acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong likewise Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guards, and Acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Palace Secretariat and General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Cavalry; Lu Chu also Director of the Palace Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards; Guo Wenyi Vice Director of the Palace Secretariat; Zhao Changwen Vice Director of the Yellow Gate—they were entrusted with state affairs, granted golden-script iron tallies, and the tallies were stored in the inner palace.
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da was made Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Right Wing Guards, and acting Minister of Rites; Wang Shichong likewise Director of the Chancellery, General-in-Chief of the Left Wing Guards, and acting Minister of Personnel; Yuan Wendu Director of the Palace Secretariat and General-in-Chief of the Left Martial Cavalry; Lu Chu also Director of the Palace Secretariat; Huangfu Wuyi Minister of War and General-in-Chief of the Right Martial Guards; Guo Wenyi and Zhao Changwen as vice directors—they were entrusted with state affairs, granted iron tallies inscribed in gold, and the tallies were kept in the inner palace.

sentences.zh: 于時洛陽稱段達等為「七貴」。

translations.literal: At that time Luoyang called Duan Da and the others the "Seven Nobles."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Luoyang called Duan Da and his colleagues the "Seven Nobles."

sentences.zh: 未幾，宇文化及立秦王子浩為天子，來次彭城，所經城邑多從逆黨。

translations.literal: Before long Yuwen Huaji set up Prince Hao of Qin as emperor and advanced to camp at Pengcheng; many of the cities along his route joined the rebel faction.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuwen Huaji installed Prince Hao of Qin as emperor and marched to camp at Pengcheng; many cities along his route went over to the rebels.

sentences.zh: 侗懼，遣使者蓋琮、馬公政招懷李密。

translations.literal: Tong was afraid and sent envoys Gai Cong and Ma Gongzheng to win over Li Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Fearing for the situation, Tong sent envoys Gai Cong and Ma Gongzheng to win Li Mi over.

sentences.zh: 密遂遣使請降，侗大悅，禮其使甚厚。

translations.literal: Li Mi thereupon sent envoys to offer submission; Tong was greatly pleased and treated his envoys with great honor.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi then sent envoys to offer submission. Tong was overjoyed and treated the envoys with great honor.

sentences.zh: 即拜密為太尉、尚書令、魏國公，令拒化及。

translations.literal: He at once appointed Li Mi Grand Marshal, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Wei, and ordered him to resist Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately appointed Li Mi Grand Marshal, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Wei, and ordered him to resist Huaji.

sentences.zh: 下書曰：

translations.literal: An edict was issued, which read:
translations.idiomatic: An edict was issued, which read:

sentences.zh: :我大隋之有天下，於茲三十八載。

translations.literal: Our Great Sui has possessed the realm for thirty-eight years to this day.
translations.idiomatic: Our Great Sui has held the realm for thirty-eight years now.

sentences.zh: 高祖文皇帝聖略神功，載造區夏。

translations.literal: The High Ancestor, Emperor Wen, by sacred strategy and divine achievement recreated the central realm.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen, the High Ancestor, by sacred strategy and divine power recreated the central realm.

sentences.zh: 世祖明皇帝則天法地，混一華戎。

translations.literal: The Shizu, Emperor Ming, modeled himself on heaven and earth and united Chinese and barbarian.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming, the Shizu, took heaven and earth as his model and united Chinese and foreign peoples under one rule.

sentences.zh: 東暨蟠木，西通細柳，前逾丹徼，後越幽都。

translations.literal: East to Panmu, west to Xiliu; south beyond the red frontier, north past Youdu.
translations.idiomatic: East to Panmu, west to Xiliu; south beyond the southern marches, north past Youdu.

sentences.zh: 日月之所臨，風雨之所至，圓首方足，稟氣食芼，莫不盡入提封，皆為臣妾。

translations.literal: Wherever sun and moon shine, wherever wind and rain reach—all round-headed, square-footed beings who receive breath and eat vegetation—none failed to enter the measured bounds; all became subjects.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever sun and moon shine, wherever wind and rain reach—all who draw breath and live upon the earth—none failed to enter the imperial domain; all became subjects.

sentences.zh: 加以寶貺畢集，靈瑞咸臻，作樂制禮，移風易俗。

translations.literal: Moreover precious tributes gathered in full; numinous omens all arrived; music was composed and rites established; customs were transformed.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover precious tributes poured in; auspicious omens appeared on every side; music was composed and rites established; customs were transformed throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 智周寰海，萬物鹹受其賜，道濟天下，百姓用而不知。

translations.literal: Wisdom encompassed the seas; the myriad things all received his bounty; the Way aided the world, and the common people benefited without knowing it.
translations.idiomatic: His wisdom encompassed the seas; the myriad things all received his bounty; his Way sustained the world, and the people benefited without even knowing it.

sentences.zh: 世祖往因曆試，統臨南服，自居皇極，順茲望幸。

translations.literal: The Shizu formerly, through successive trials, governed the southern domains; once he ascended the imperial pinnacle, he followed this with tours of inspection.
translations.idiomatic: The Shizu had formerly, through successive appointments, governed the southern regions; once he took the throne, he continued with tours of inspection as the people desired.

sentences.zh: 所以往歲省方，展禮肆覲，停鑾駐蹕，按駕清道，八屯如昔，七萃不移。

translations.literal: Therefore in years past he inspected the regions, displayed rites and received homage; the imperial carriage halted and the procession paused; escorts cleared the road; the eight encampments stood as before and the seven guards did not stir.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore in years past he toured the provinces, displayed the rites and received homage; the imperial carriage halted and the procession paused; escorts cleared the road; the palace guards stood as before and did not stir.

sentences.zh: 豈意釁起非常，逮於軒陛，災生不意，延及冕旒。

translations.literal: Who could have thought that calamity would arise beyond the ordinary, reaching the imperial hall, and disaster strike unlooked-for, extending to the imperial crown?
translations.idiomatic: Who could have thought that rebellion would arise beyond all expectation, reaching the imperial hall, and disaster strike unlooked-for, touching the imperial crown itself?

sentences.zh: 奉諱之日，五情崩隕，攀號荼毒，不能自勝。

translations.literal: On the day I received the mournful tidings, my five emotions collapsed; I cried out in anguish and could not master myself.
translations.idiomatic: On the day I received the mournful tidings, my heart gave way; I cried out in anguish and could not master my grief.

sentences.zh: :且聞之，自古代有屯剝，賊臣逆子，無世無之。

translations.literal: Moreover I have heard that from antiquity there have been times of hardship; treacherous ministers and rebellious sons exist in no age without them.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover it is said that from antiquity there have been times of hardship; treacherous ministers and rebellious sons have existed in every age.

sentences.zh: 至如宇文化及，世傳庸品。

translations.literal: As for Yuwen Huaji, the world has handed down the report that he is a mediocre sort.
translations.idiomatic: As for Yuwen Huaji, the world has long regarded him as a man of mediocre talent.

sentences.zh: 其父述，往屬時來，早沾厚遇，賜以婚媾，置之公輔，位尊九命，祿重萬鐘，禮極人臣，榮冠世表。

translations.literal: His father Shu, when the times favored him, early received generous treatment: granted marriage alliance, placed among chief ministers, rank honored with the nine orders, stipend heavy with ten thousand piculs, rites reaching the utmost for a subject, glory crowning his generation.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu, when fortune favored him, received generous treatment early on: he was granted a marriage alliance with the imperial house, placed among the chief ministers, honored with the highest rank, paid a stipend of ten thousand piculs, accorded the utmost rites due a subject, and his glory crowned his generation.

sentences.zh: 徒承海嶽之恩，未有涓塵之益。

translations.literal: They merely received favor vast as seas and mountains, yet rendered no benefit even the size of a drop or mote of dust.
translations.idiomatic: They merely received favor vast as seas and mountains, yet rendered no benefit even the size of a drop of water or grain of dust.

sentences.zh: 化及以此下材，夙蒙顧盼，出入外內，奉望階墀。

translations.literal: Huaji, with this inferior talent, long enjoyed the imperial gaze, passing in and out of the inner and outer courts and attending upon the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji, for all his inferior talent, long enjoyed the emperor's favor, passing in and out of the inner and outer courts and attending upon the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 昔陪籓國，統領禁衛，及從升皇祚，陪列九卿。

translations.literal: Formerly he attended the princely domain and commanded the palace guards; when the emperor ascended the throne, he took rank among the Nine Ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly he served in the princely household and commanded the palace guards; when the emperor took the throne, he took rank among the Nine Ministers.

sentences.zh: 但本性兇狠，恣其貪穢，或交結惡黨，或侵掠貨財，事重刑篇，狀盈獄簡。

translations.literal: But by nature he was fierce and cruel, indulging his greed and corruption—now consorting with evil factions, now plundering goods and wealth—matters grave under the penal code, charges filling the prison records.
translations.idiomatic: But by nature he was fierce and cruel, indulging his greed and corruption—now consorting with evil factions, now plundering goods and wealth—offenses grave under the penal code, charges filling the prison records.

sentences.zh: 在上不遺簪履，恩加草芥，應至死辜，每蒙恕免。

translations.literal: The sovereign did not cast away even hairpin and shoes; his grace extended even to grass and husks—though deserving death, he was each time pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: The sovereign did not cast him off even for the smallest offense; his grace extended even to the lowliest—though deserving death, he was pardoned again and again.

sentences.zh: 三經除解，尋複本職，再徙邊裔，仍即追還。

translations.literal: Three times he was dismissed from office, yet soon restored to his former post; twice banished to the frontier, yet immediately recalled.
translations.idiomatic: Three times he was dismissed from office, yet soon restored to his former post; twice banished to the frontier, yet immediately recalled.

sentences.zh: 生成之恩，昊天罔極，獎擢之義，人事罕聞。

translations.literal: The grace of giving him life was boundless as heaven; the principle of promoting and elevating him is rarely heard of among men.
translations.idiomatic: The grace of giving him life was boundless as heaven; such promotion and favor is rarely heard of among men.

sentences.zh: 化及梟獍為心，禽獸不若，縱毒興禍，傾覆行宮。

translations.literal: Huaji had the heart of an owl or a jackal—worse than beasts; he unleashed poison and raised calamity, overthrowing the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji had the heart of an owl or a jackal—worse than any beast; he unleashed poison and raised calamity, overthrowing the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 諸王兄弟，一時殘酷，痛暴行路，世不忍言。

translations.literal: The princely brothers were slaughtered in a single moment with cruel violence; the anguish on the roads was such that the age cannot bear to speak of it.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial princes were slaughtered in a single moment with cruel violence; the anguish on the roads was such that the age cannot bear to speak of it.

sentences.zh: 有窮之在夏時，犬戎之于周代，釁辱之極，亦未是過。

translations.literal: The outrage of Youqiong in the Xia age, the Dog Rong in the Zhou era—even the utmost of insult and shame did not surpass this.
translations.idiomatic: The outrage of Youqiong in the Xia age, the Dog Rong in the Zhou era—even the utmost of insult and shame did not surpass this.

sentences.zh: 朕所以刻骨崩心，飲膽嘗血，瞻天視地，無處容身。

translations.literal: Therefore I have carved this into my bones and shattered my heart, drunk gall and tasted blood, looked up to heaven and down to earth, and found nowhere to hide my person.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore I have carved this into my bones and shattered my heart, drunk gall and tasted blood, looked up to heaven and down to earth, and found nowhere to hide my shame.

sentences.zh: :今王公卿士，庶僚百辟，鹹以大寶鴻名，不可顛墜，元兇巨猾，須早夷殄，翼戴朕躬，嗣守寶位。

translations.literal: Now the princes, dukes, ministers, and scholars, and the hundred ranks of officials, all hold that the great treasure and august name must not be overturned, that the chief villain and great rogue must soon be exterminated, and that they should support and raise me to succeed in guarding the precious throne.
translations.idiomatic: Now the princes, ministers, and officials of every rank all hold that the great treasure of the throne and the august imperial name must not fall, that the chief villain must soon be destroyed, and that they should support me in succeeding to guard the throne.

sentences.zh: 顧惟寡薄，志不逮此。

translations.literal: Looking upon my own meager worth, my will does not reach to this.
translations.idiomatic: Considering my own meager worth, my will does not reach to this.

sentences.zh: 今者出黼扆而杖旄鉞，釋衰麻而擐甲胄，銜冤誓眾，忍淚治兵，指日遄征，以平大盜。

translations.literal: Now I leave the embroidered screen and take up battle-axes and halberds, cast off mourning hemp and don armor, harbor my grievance and swear the host, choke back tears and marshal troops, and within days shall march swiftly to pacify the great bandit.
translations.idiomatic: Now I leave the throne and take up battle-axes and halberds, cast off mourning garb and don armor, harbor my grievance and swear the host, choke back tears and marshal troops, and within days shall march swiftly to pacify the great rebel.

sentences.zh: 且化及偽立秦王之子，幽遏比於囚拘，其身自稱霸相，專擅擬於九五。

translations.literal: Moreover Huaji has falsely set up the son of the Prince of Qin, holding him in confinement like a prisoner, while he himself styles himself overlord and chancellor and arrogates authority fitting the Son of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Huaji has falsely installed the son of the Prince of Qin, holding him in confinement like a prisoner, while he himself styles himself overlord and chancellor and arrogates the authority of the Son of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 履踐禁禦，據有宮闈，昂首揚眉，初無慚色。

translations.literal: He treads the forbidden precincts and occupies the palace inner quarters, raising his head and arching his brows without the slightest shame.
translations.idiomatic: He treads the forbidden precincts and occupies the palace inner quarters, raising his head and arching his brows without the slightest shame.

sentences.zh: 衣冠朝望，外懼凶威，志士誠臣，內皆憤怨。

translations.literal: The court officials and men of standing outwardly fear his fierce power, while men of resolve and loyal ministers inwardly seethe with anger and resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The court officials outwardly fear his fierce power, while men of resolve and loyal ministers inwardly seethe with anger and resentment.

sentences.zh: 以我義師，順彼天道，梟夷醜族，匪夕伊朝。

translations.literal: With our righteous army, following heaven's way, we shall behead and exterminate the vile clan—not one evening but one morning away.
translations.idiomatic: With our righteous army, following heaven's way, we shall behead and exterminate the vile clan—not in an evening but in a morning.

sentences.zh: :太尉、尚書令、魏公丹誠內發，宏略外舉，率勤王之師，討違天之逆。

translations.literal: The Grand Marshal, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Wei, with crimson loyalty issuing from within and grand strategy displayed without, leads the army that would rescue the throne to punish the rebel who defies heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Marshal, Director of the Department of State Affairs, and Duke of Wei, with loyal devotion in his heart and grand strategy in his conduct, leads the army that would rescue the throne to punish the rebel who defies heaven.

sentences.zh: 果毅爭先，熊羆競逐，金鼓振讋，若火焚毛，鋒刃縱橫，如湯沃雪。

translations.literal: The resolute vie to take the lead; bears and brown bears race in pursuit; drums and gongs shake the craven as fire burns hair; blades cross like boiling water poured on snow.
translations.idiomatic: The resolute vie to take the lead; warriors race in pursuit; drums and gongs shake the craven as fire burns hair; blades cross like boiling water poured on snow.

sentences.zh: 魏公志在匡濟，投袂前驅，朕親禦六軍，星言繼進。

translations.literal: The Duke of Wei's aim is to set the realm right; he flings up his sleeves and advances in the van; I myself shall command the six armies and march swiftly in his wake.
translations.idiomatic: The Duke of Wei's aim is to set the realm right; he flings up his sleeves and advances in the van; I myself shall command the six armies and march swiftly in his wake.

sentences.zh: 以此眾戰，以斯順舉，擘山可以動，射石可以入。

translations.literal: With such a host fighting, with such a righteous undertaking, one could move a mountain by splitting it and pierce stone with an arrow.
translations.idiomatic: With such an army fighting, with such a righteous cause, one could move mountains and pierce stone with an arrow.

sentences.zh: 況擁此人徒，皆有離德，京都侍衛，西憶鄉家，江左淳民，南思邦邑，比來表書駱驛，人信相尋。

translations.literal: Moreover those who follow this man all harbor divided loyalties; the capital guards long westward for their home villages; the plain folk of the Jiang left yearn south for their native districts; recently memorials and letters have come in ceaseless streams, and messengers follow one upon another.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover those who follow this man all harbor divided loyalties; the capital guards long for their home villages in the west; the plain folk of the Jiang left yearn for their native districts in the south; recently memorials and letters have come in ceaseless streams, and messengers follow one upon another.

sentences.zh: 若王師一臨，舊章暫睹，自應解甲倒戈，冰銷葉散。

translations.literal: If the royal army arrives once, and they briefly behold the old order, they will of themselves cast off armor and turn their weapons, melting like ice and scattering like leaves.
translations.idiomatic: If the royal army arrives once, and they briefly behold the old order restored, they will of themselves cast off armor and turn their weapons, melting like ice and scattering like leaves.

sentences.zh: 且聞化及自恣，天奪其心，殺戮不辜，挫辱人士，莫不道路仄目，號天踞地。

translations.literal: Moreover I hear that Huaji indulges himself at will; heaven has taken away his mind; he slaughters the innocent and humiliates men of standing—none but narrow their eyes on the roads and cry to heaven and stamp the earth.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover I hear that Huaji indulges himself at will; heaven has taken away his mind; he slaughters the innocent and humiliates men of standing—everyone on the roads narrows his eyes in anger and cries to heaven and stamps the earth.

sentences.zh: 朕今復仇雪恥，梟轘者一人，拯溺救焚，所哀者士庶。

translations.literal: I now take revenge and wash away shame; only one man shall be beheaded and exposed; I rescue the drowning and save those in fire—the ones I pity are the scholars and common people.
translations.idiomatic: I now take revenge and wash away shame; only one man shall be beheaded and exposed; I rescue the drowning and save those in fire—the ones I pity are the scholars and common people.

sentences.zh: 唯天鑒孔殷，祐我宗社，億兆感義，俱會朕心。

translations.literal: May heaven look down with deep compassion and protect our altars of soil and grain; the hundred millions, moved by righteousness, all join with my heart.
translations.idiomatic: May heaven look down with deep compassion and protect our altars of soil and grain; the hundred millions, moved by righteousness, all join with my heart.

sentences.zh: 梟戮元兇，策勳飲至，四海交泰，稱朕意焉。

translations.literal: When the chief villain is beheaded and exposed, merits are recorded and the celebratory toast is drunk, and the four seas are at peace together—then my wish will be fulfilled.
translations.idiomatic: When the chief villain is beheaded and exposed, merits are recorded and the celebratory toast is drunk, and the four seas are at peace together—then my wish will be fulfilled.

sentences.zh: 兵術軍機，並受魏公節度。

translations.literal: All military arts and army affairs shall be subject to the Duke of Wei's command.
translations.idiomatic: All military arts and army affairs shall be subject to the Duke of Wei's command.

sentences.zh: 密見使者，大悅，北面拜伏，臣禮甚恭。

translations.literal: When Li Mi saw the envoys he was greatly pleased, faced north, bowed prostrate, and performed the ceremonies of a subject with great reverence.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Mi saw the envoys he was overjoyed, faced north, bowed prostrate, and performed the ceremonies of a subject with great reverence.

sentences.zh: 密遂東拒化及。

translations.literal: Li Mi thereupon marched east to resist Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: Li Mi thereupon marched east to resist Huaji.

sentences.zh: 「七貴」頗不協，陰有相圖之計。

translations.literal: The "Seven Nobles" were rather at odds and secretly plotted against one another.
translations.idiomatic: The "Seven Nobles" were rather at odds and secretly plotted against one another.

sentences.zh: 未幾，元文都、盧楚、郭文懿、趙長文等為世充所殺，皇甫無逸遁歸長安。

translations.literal: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Shichong; Huangfu Wuyi fled and returned to Chang'an.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Yuan Wendu, Lu Chu, Guo Wenyi, Zhao Changwen, and others were killed by Shichong; Huangfu Wuyi fled back to Chang'an.

sentences.zh: 世充詣侗所陳謝，辭情哀苦。

translations.literal: Shichong went to Tong's residence to offer apology; his words were piteous and anguished.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong went to Tong's residence to apologize; his words were piteous and anguished.

sentences.zh: 侗以為至誠，命之上殿，被發為盟，誓無貳志。

translations.literal: Tong took this as utmost sincerity, ordered him up to the hall, and with loose hair they made a covenant, swearing he had no second intent.
translations.idiomatic: Tong took this as utmost sincerity, summoned him to the hall, and with hair unbound they made a covenant, swearing he had no second intent.

sentences.zh: 自是侗無所關預。

translations.literal: From this time Tong had no part in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From this time Tong had no part in affairs.

sentences.zh: 侗心不能平，遂與記室陸士季謀圖世充，事不果而止。

translations.literal: Tong's heart could not be at peace; he then joined with Recorder Lu Shiji in plotting against Shichong, but the affair did not succeed and was abandoned.
translations.idiomatic: Tong's heart could not be at peace; he then joined with his recorder Lu Shiji in plotting against Shichong, but the affair did not succeed and was abandoned.

sentences.zh: 及世充破李密，眾望益歸之，遂自為鄭王，總百揆，加九錫，備法物，侗不能禁也。

translations.literal: When Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular expectation turned increasingly to him; he thereupon made himself Prince of Zheng, took charge of all government, received the Nine Bestowals, and prepared the ritual regalia—and Tong could not stop him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shichong defeated Li Mi, popular expectation turned increasingly to him; he thereupon made himself Prince of Zheng, took charge of all government, received the Nine Bestowals, and prepared the ritual regalia—and Tong could not stop him.

sentences.zh: 段達、雲定興等十人入見於侗曰：「天命不常，鄭王功德甚盛，願陛下揖讓告禪，遵唐、虞之跡。

translations.literal: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others entered to see Tong and said: "The Mandate of Heaven is not constant; the Prince of Zheng's merit and virtue are very great. We beg Your Majesty to yield by bowing and announce abdication, following the traces of Tang and Yu."
translations.idiomatic: Duan Da, Yun Dingxing, and ten others came before Tong and said, "The Mandate of Heaven is not constant; the Prince of Zheng's merit and virtue are very great. We beg Your Majesty to yield the throne and announce abdication, following the example of Tang and Yu."

sentences.zh: 」侗聞之怒曰：「天下者，高祖之天下，東都者，世祖之東都。

translations.literal: " When Tong heard this he said in anger: "The realm belongs to the High Ancestor; the Eastern Capital belongs to the Shizu."
translations.idiomatic: " When Tong heard this he said in anger, "The realm belongs to Emperor Wen; the Eastern Capital belongs to Emperor Yang."

sentences.zh: 若隋德未衰，此言不可發；

translations.literal: If Sui virtue has not yet declined, such words must not be spoken;
translations.idiomatic: If Sui virtue has not yet declined, such words must not be spoken;

sentences.zh: 必天命有改，亦何論於禪讓！

translations.literal: even if the Mandate has changed, what talk is there of abdication!
translations.idiomatic: even if the Mandate has changed, what talk is there of abdication!

sentences.zh: 公等或先朝舊臣，績宣上代，或勤王立節，身服軒冕，忽有斯言，朕複當何所望！

translations.literal: You gentlemen are either old ministers of the former court who displayed merit in the previous reign, or men who upheld the throne with loyal resolve and wear court robes—suddenly to have such words, what may I still hope for!
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen are either old ministers of the former court who served the previous reign with merit, or men who upheld the throne with loyal resolve and wear court robes—suddenly to speak such words, what may I still hope for!

sentences.zh: 」神色懍然，侍衛者莫不流汗。

translations.literal: " His expression was stern; none of the attendants but broke into a sweat.
translations.idiomatic: " His expression was stern; every attendant broke into a sweat.

sentences.zh: 既而退朝，對良娣而泣。

translations.literal: Afterward he left court and wept before the Worthy Companion.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he left court and wept before his mother, the Worthy Companion.

sentences.zh: 世充更使人謂侗曰：「今海內未定，須得長君。

translations.literal: Shichong again sent someone to say to Tong: "Now the realm within the seas is not settled; a mature ruler is needed.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong again sent someone to say to Tong, "The realm is not yet settled; a mature ruler is needed.

sentences.zh: 待四方乂安，複子明辟，必若前盟，義不違負。

translations.literal: When the four quarters are at peace, I shall restore you to the bright throne; as in our former covenant, in righteousness I shall not break faith."
translations.idiomatic: When the four quarters are at peace, I shall restore you to the throne; as in our former covenant, in righteousness I shall not break faith."

sentences.zh: 」侗不得已，遜位於世充，遂被幽於含涼殿。

translations.literal: " Tong had no choice; he yielded the throne to Shichong and was then confined in the Hanliang Hall.
translations.idiomatic: " Tong had no choice; he yielded the throne to Shichong and was then confined in the Hanliang Hall.

sentences.zh: 世充僭偽號，封為潞國公，邑五千戶。

translations.literal: Shichong usurped the imperial title and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu with a fief of five thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong usurped the imperial title and enfeoffed him as Duke of Lu with a fief of five thousand households.

sentences.zh: 月餘，宇文儒童、裴仁基等謀誅世充，複尊立侗，事泄，並見害。

translations.literal: After more than a month Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Shichong and restore Tong to the throne; the affair was exposed and they were all killed.
translations.idiomatic: After more than a month Yuwen Rutong, Pei Renji, and others plotted to kill Shichong and restore Tong to the throne; the affair was exposed and they were all killed.

sentences.zh: 世充兄世惲因勸世充害侗，以絕民望。

translations.literal: Shichong's elder brother Shiyun thereupon urged Shichong to kill Tong in order to cut off popular expectation.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong's elder brother Shiyun thereupon urged Shichong to kill Tong in order to cut off popular hope in the Sui line.

sentences.zh: 世充遣其侄行本齎鴆詣侗所曰：「願皇帝飲此酒。

translations.literal: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben bearing poison to Tong's residence, saying: "I beg the emperor to drink this wine."
translations.idiomatic: Shichong sent his nephew Xingben bearing poison to Tong's residence, saying, "I beg the emperor to drink this wine."

sentences.zh: 」侗知不免，請與母相見，不許。

translations.literal: " Tong knew he could not escape; he begged to see his mother and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: " Tong knew he could not escape; he begged to see his mother and was refused.

sentences.zh: 遂布席焚香禮佛，咒曰：「從今以去，願不生帝王尊貴之家。

translations.literal: He then spread a mat, burned incense, and worshiped the Buddha, praying: "From this time forward, may I never be born into an imperial or exalted house."
translations.idiomatic: He then spread a mat, burned incense, and worshiped the Buddha, praying, "From this time forward, may I never be born into an imperial or exalted house."

sentences.zh: 」於是仰藥。

translations.literal: " He then drank the poison.
translations.idiomatic: " He then drank the poison.

sentences.zh: 不能時絕，更以帛縊之。

translations.literal: He did not die at once, and they further strangled him with silk.
translations.idiomatic: He did not die at once, and they strangled him with silk.

sentences.zh: 世充偽諡為恭皇帝。

translations.literal: Shichong falsely gave him the posthumous title Emperor Gong.
translations.idiomatic: Shichong falsely gave him the posthumous title Emperor Gong.

sentences.zh: 齊王齊王暕，字世朏，小字阿孩。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi Zheng, styled Shifu, childhood name Ahai—the text repeats the title—
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zheng of Qi, whose style name was Shifu and childhood name Ahai,

sentences.zh: 美容儀，疏眉目，少為高祖所愛。

translations.literal: was handsome in bearing with well-spaced brows and eyes; from youth he was loved by the High Ancestor.
translations.idiomatic: was handsome in bearing with well-spaced brows and eyes; from youth he was loved by Emperor Wen.

sentences.zh: 開皇中，立為豫章王，邑千戶。

translations.literal: During the Kaihuang era he was invested as Prince of Yuzhang with a fief of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: During the Kaihuang era he was made Prince of Yuzhang with a fief of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 及長，頗涉經史，尤工騎射。

translations.literal: When he grew up he ranged widely through the classics and histories and was especially skilled at mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: When he grew up he studied the classics and histories widely and was especially skilled at mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 初為內史令。

translations.literal: At first he was Director of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At first he served as Director of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，拜揚州總管沿淮以南諸軍事。

translations.literal: During Renshou he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou and military affairs south of the Huai.
translations.idiomatic: During the Renshou era he was appointed Commander-in-Chief of Yangzhou with authority over military affairs south of the Huai.

sentences.zh: 煬帝即位，進封齊王，增邑四千戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was advanced to Prince of Qi and his fief was increased by four thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Yang took the throne, he was advanced to Prince of Qi and his fief was increased by four thousand households.

sentences.zh: ，帝初入東都，盛陳鹵簿，暕為軍導。

translations.literal: When the emperor first entered the Eastern Capital, the imperial guard of honor was displayed in full splendor, and Zheng served as military vanguard.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor first entered the Eastern Capital, the imperial guard of honor was displayed in full splendor, and Zheng served as military vanguard.

sentences.zh: 尋轉豫州牧。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to Governor of Yu Province.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Governor of Yu Province.

sentences.zh: 俄而元德太子薨，朝野注望，鹹以暕當嗣。

translations.literal: Before long the Yuande Heir Apparent died; court and countryside fixed their hopes on Zheng, all holding that he should succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Yuande Heir Apparent died; court and countryside fixed their hopes on Zheng, believing he would be named heir.

sentences.zh: 帝又敕吏部尚書牛弘妙選官屬，公卿由是多進子弟。

translations.literal: The emperor also ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to select excellent staff; the chief ministers therefore mostly advanced their sons and younger relatives.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also ordered Minister of Personnel Niu Hong to select excellent staff for him; the chief ministers therefore mostly advanced their sons and younger relatives.

sentences.zh: 明年，轉雍州牧，尋徙河南尹、開府儀同三司。

translations.literal: The next year he was transferred to Governor of Yong Province, and soon moved to Intendant of Henan and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Three Honors.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Governor of Yong Province, and soon became Intendant of Henan and Grand Master for Splendid Happiness with the Three Honors.

sentences.zh: 元德太子左右二萬餘人悉隸於暕，寵遇益隆，自樂平公主及諸戚屬競來致禮，百官稱謁，填咽道路。

translations.literal: More than twenty thousand attendants of the Yuande Heir Apparent all came under Zheng's command; his favor grew ever greater; from the Princess of Leping and all the kin, gifts were offered in rivalry; officials paid their respects until the roads were choked.
translations.idiomatic: More than twenty thousand attendants of the Yuande Heir Apparent all came under Zheng's command; his favor grew ever greater; from the Princess of Leping and all the imperial kin, gifts poured in; officials paid their respects until the roads were choked.

sentences.zh: 暕頗驕恣，昵近小人，所行多不法，遣喬令則、劉虔安、裴該、皇甫諶、庫狄仲錡、陳智偉等求聲色狗馬。

translations.literal: Zheng was rather arrogant and willful, intimate with petty men; much of what he did was unlawful. He sent Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, Kudi Zhongqi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to seek music, women, dogs, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was arrogant and willful, intimate with petty men; much of what he did was unlawful. He sent Qiao Lingze, Liu Qian'an, Pei Gai, Huangfu Chen, Kudi Zhongqi, Chen Zhiwei, and others to seek music, women, dogs, and horses.

sentences.zh: 令則等因此放縱，訪人家有女者，輒矯暕命呼之，載入暕宅，因緣藏隱，恣行淫穢，而後遣之。

translations.literal: Lingze and the others therefore ran wild; wherever they found a household with a daughter, they would forge Zheng's order to summon her, carry her into Zheng's residence, hide her by various pretexts, indulge in debauchery at will, and only then send her away.
translations.idiomatic: Lingze and the others therefore ran wild; wherever they found a household with a daughter, they would forge Zheng's order to summon her, carry her into his residence, hide her by various pretexts, indulge in debauchery at will, and only then send her away.

sentences.zh: 仲錡、智偉二人詣隴西，撾炙諸胡，責其名馬，得數匹以進於。

translations.literal: Zhongqi and Zhiwei two men went to Longxi, beat and roasted various foreigners, demanded their famous horses, and obtained several steeds to present to him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhongqi and Zhiwei went to Longxi, abused the foreign traders there, demanded their famous horses, and obtained several steeds to present to Zheng.

sentences.zh: 暕令還主，仲錡等詐言王賜，將歸於家，暕不之知也。

translations.literal: Zheng ordered them returned to their owners; Zhongqi and the others falsely claimed the prince had bestowed the horses and took them home—Zheng did not know of this.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng ordered the horses returned to their owners; Zhongqi and the others falsely claimed the prince had bestowed them and took them home—Zheng knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 又樂平公主嘗奏帝，言柳氏女美者，帝未有所答。

translations.literal: Moreover the Princess of Leping once reported to the emperor that a daughter of the Liu clan was beautiful; the emperor made no reply.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover the Princess of Leping once told the emperor that a daughter of the Liu clan was beautiful; the emperor made no reply.

sentences.zh: 久之，主複以柳氏進於暕，暕習納之。

translations.literal: After a long time the princess again presented the Liu girl to Zheng, and Zheng readily took her in.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time the princess again presented the Liu girl to Zheng, and he readily took her in.

sentences.zh: 其後帝問主柳氏女所在，主曰：「在齊王所。

translations.literal: Later the emperor asked the princess where the Liu girl was; the princess said: "She is at the Prince of Qi's residence."
translations.idiomatic: Later the emperor asked the princess where the Liu girl was; the princess said, "She is at Prince Zheng of Qi's residence."

sentences.zh: 」帝不悅。

translations.literal: " The emperor was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor was displeased.

sentences.zh: 暕于東都營第，大門無故而崩，聽事栿中折，識者以為不祥。

translations.literal: When Zheng was building a residence in the Eastern Capital, the main gate collapsed for no reason and the central beam of the reception hall broke in two; those who understood such things took it as ill omen.
translations.idiomatic: When Zheng was building a residence in the Eastern Capital, the main gate collapsed for no reason and the central beam of the reception hall broke in two; those who understood such things took it as an ill omen.

sentences.zh: 其後從帝幸榆林，暕督後軍步騎五萬，恆與帝相去數十裡而舍。

translations.literal: Afterward he followed the emperor to Yulin; Zheng commanded the rear army of fifty thousand foot and horse, always encamping several tens of li from the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Afterward he followed the emperor to Yulin; Zheng commanded the rear army of fifty thousand foot and horse, always encamping several tens of li from the emperor.

sentences.zh: 會帝于汾陽宮大獵，詔暕以千騎入圍。

translations.literal: When the emperor held a great hunt at Fenyang Palace, he ordered Zheng to enter the hunting enclosure with a thousand horsemen.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor held a great hunt at Fenyang Palace, he ordered Zheng to enter the hunting enclosure with a thousand horsemen.

sentences.zh: 暕大獲麋鹿以獻，而帝未有得也，乃怒從官，皆言為暕左右所遏，獸不得前。

translations.literal: Zheng took many elk and deer and presented them, but the emperor had caught nothing; he thereupon raged at his attendants, who all said Zheng's men had blocked the way and the game could not advance.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng took many elk and deer and presented them, but the emperor had caught nothing; he raged at his attendants, who all said Zheng's men had blocked the way and kept the game from reaching the emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝於是發怒，求暕罪失。

translations.literal: The emperor thereupon grew angry and sought out Zheng's offenses.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon grew angry and sought out Zheng's offenses.

sentences.zh: 時制縣令無故不得出境，有伊闕令皇甫詡幸於暕，違禁將之汾陽宮。

translations.literal: At that time the rule was that magistrates might not leave their districts without cause; the magistrate of Yique, Huangfu Xu, who enjoyed Zheng's favor, violated the prohibition and took him to Fenyang Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At that time magistrates might not leave their districts without cause; Huangfu Xu, magistrate of Yique, who enjoyed Zheng's favor, violated the prohibition and accompanied him to Fenyang Palace.

sentences.zh: 又京兆人達奚通有妾王氏善歌，貴遊宴聚，多或要致，於是輾轉亦出入王家。

translations.literal: Moreover Daxi Tong of Jingzhao had a concubine, Lady Wang, skilled in song; at banquets of the noble and powerful many would request her presence, and so by turns she also came and went at the Wang residence.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Daxi Tong of Jingzhao had a concubine, Lady Wang, skilled in song; at banquets of the noble and powerful many would request her, and so by turns she also came and went at Zheng's residence.

sentences.zh: 禦史韋德裕希旨劾暕，帝令甲士千餘大索暕第，因窮治其事。

translations.literal: Censor Wei Deyu, following the emperor's intent, impeached Zheng; the emperor ordered more than a thousand armored soldiers to search Zheng's residence thoroughly and pursued the matter to its full extent.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Wei Deyu, following the emperor's intent, impeached Zheng; the emperor ordered more than a thousand armored soldiers to search his residence thoroughly and pursued the matter to its full extent.

sentences.zh: 暕妃韋氏者，民部尚書沖之女也，早卒，暕遂與妃姊元氏婦通，遂產一女，外人皆不得知。

translations.literal: Zheng's consort was of the Wei clan, daughter of Minister of the Household Chong; she died early, and Zheng then had relations with his consort's elder sister, wife of the Yuan clan, and she bore a daughter—outsiders knew nothing of it.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng's consort was Lady Wei, daughter of Minister of the Household Chong; she died young, and Zheng then had relations with his consort's elder sister, wife of the Yuan clan, who bore a daughter—outsiders knew nothing of it.

sentences.zh: 陰引喬令則於第內酣宴，令則稱慶，脫暕帽以為歡樂。

translations.literal: He secretly brought Qiao Lingze into the residence for a drunken feast; Lingze offered congratulations and removed Zheng's cap for merriment.
translations.idiomatic: He secretly brought Qiao Lingze into the residence for a drunken feast; Lingze offered congratulations and removed Zheng's cap in celebration.

sentences.zh: 召相工令遍視後庭，相工指妃姊曰：「此產子者當為皇后。

translations.literal: He summoned a physiognomist to inspect the entire rear court; the physiognomist pointed to the consort's sister and said: "She who has borne a child shall become empress."
translations.idiomatic: He summoned a physiognomist to inspect the entire rear court; the physiognomist pointed to the consort's sister and said, "She who has borne a child shall become empress."

sentences.zh: 王貴不可言。

translations.literal: The prince's honor is beyond words."
translations.idiomatic: The prince's honor is beyond words."

sentences.zh: 」時國無儲副，暕自謂次當得立。

translations.literal: " At that time the state had no heir apparent; Zheng considered himself next in line to be established.
translations.idiomatic: " At that time the state had no heir apparent; Zheng considered himself next in line for the succession.

sentences.zh: 又以元德太子有三子，內常不安，陰挾左道，為厭勝之事。

translations.literal: Moreover, because the Yuande Heir Apparent had three sons, he was inwardly never at ease and secretly employed heterodox arts to perform rites of magical suppression.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, because the Yuande Heir Apparent had three sons, he was inwardly uneasy and secretly employed heterodox arts to perform rites of magical suppression.

sentences.zh: 至是，事皆發，帝大怒，斬令則等數人，妃姊賜死，暕府僚皆斥之邊遠。

translations.literal: At this point all the matters came to light; the emperor was greatly angered, executed Lingze and several others, ordered the consort's sister to take her own life, and banished all of Zheng's staff to the distant frontier.
translations.idiomatic: At this point all the matters came to light; the emperor was greatly angered, executed Lingze and several others, ordered the consort's sister to take her own life, and banished all of Zheng's staff to the distant frontier.

sentences.zh: 時趙王杲猶在孩孺，帝謂侍臣曰：「朕唯有暕一子，不然者，當肆諸市朝，以明國憲也。

translations.literal: At that time Prince of Zhao Gao was still an infant; the emperor said to his attendants: "I have only Zheng as a son; otherwise I would expose him in the marketplace and make clear the laws of the state."
translations.idiomatic: At that time Prince Gao of Zhao was still an infant; the emperor said to his attendants, "I have only Zheng as a grown son; otherwise I would execute him in the marketplace and make clear the laws of the state."

sentences.zh: 」暕自是恩寵日衰，雖為京尹，不復關預時政。

translations.literal: " From this time Zheng's favor daily declined; though he was Intendant of the Capital, he no longer had any part in current government.
translations.idiomatic: " From this time Zheng's favor daily declined; though he was Intendant of the Capital, he no longer had any part in government affairs.

sentences.zh: 帝恆令武賁郎將一人監其府事，暕有微失，武賁輒奏之。

translations.literal: The emperor constantly assigned one Captain of the Martial Guard to oversee his residence affairs; if Zheng had the slightest fault, the guard would report it at once.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor constantly assigned one Captain of the Martial Guard to oversee his residence; if Zheng had the slightest fault, the guard would report it at once.

sentences.zh: 帝亦常慮暕生變，所給左右，皆以老弱，備員而已。

translations.literal: The emperor also constantly feared Zheng might stir up trouble; those assigned to attend him were all old and weak, filling posts in name only.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also constantly feared Zheng might stir up trouble; those assigned to attend him were all old and weak, filling posts in name only.

sentences.zh: 暕每懷危懼，心不自安。

translations.literal: Zheng constantly harbored fear and danger; his heart was never at peace.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng constantly lived in fear; his heart was never at peace.

sentences.zh: 又帝在江都宮，元會，暕具法服將朝，無故有血從裳中而下。

translations.literal: Moreover when the emperor was at the Jiangdu palace for the New Year audience, Zheng dressed in ceremonial robes to attend court, and for no reason blood flowed down from within his garments.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when the emperor was at the Jiangdu palace for the New Year audience, Zheng dressed in ceremonial robes to attend court, and for no reason blood flowed down from within his garments.

sentences.zh: 又坐齋中，見群鼠數十，至前而死，視皆無頭。

translations.literal: Again while seated in his study he saw several dozen rats come before him and die; when he looked, all were headless.
translations.idiomatic: Again while seated in his study he saw several dozen rats come before him and die; when he looked, all were headless.

sentences.zh: 暕意甚惡之。

translations.literal: Zheng was deeply troubled by this.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng was deeply troubled by this.

sentences.zh: 俄而化及作亂，兵將犯蹕，帝聞，顧謂蕭後曰：「得非阿孩邪？

translations.literal: Before long Huaji rose in rebellion and troops were about to assault the imperial escort; when the emperor heard, he turned to Empress Xiao and said: "Could it not be Ahai?"
translations.idiomatic: Before long Huaji rose in rebellion and troops were about to assault the imperial escort; when the emperor heard, he turned to Empress Xiao and said, "Could it not be Ahai?"

sentences.zh: 」其見疏忌如此。

translations.literal: " Such was the estrangement and suspicion with which he was regarded.
translations.idiomatic: " Such was the estrangement and suspicion with which he was regarded.

sentences.zh: 化及複令人捕暕，暕時尚臥未起，賊既進，暕驚曰：「是何人？

translations.literal: Huaji again sent men to seize Zheng; Zheng was still lying abed and had not risen; when the rebels entered, Zheng cried in alarm: "Who are you?"
translations.idiomatic: Huaji again sent men to seize Zheng; Zheng was still lying abed; when the rebels entered, he cried in alarm, "Who are you?"

sentences.zh: 」莫有報者，暕猶謂帝令捕之，因曰：「詔使且緩。

translations.literal: " No one answered; Zheng still thought the emperor had ordered his arrest, and therefore said: "Imperial envoy, wait a moment.
translations.idiomatic: " No one answered; Zheng still thought the emperor had ordered his arrest, and said, "Imperial envoy, wait a moment.

sentences.zh: 兒不負國家。

translations.literal: Your son has not betrayed the state."
translations.idiomatic: Your son has not betrayed the state."

sentences.zh: 」賊於是曳至街而斬之，及其二子亦遇害。

translations.literal: " The rebels then dragged him to the street and beheaded him; his two sons also met with harm.
translations.idiomatic: " The rebels then dragged him into the street and beheaded him; his two sons were also killed.

sentences.zh: 暕竟不知殺者為誰。

translations.literal: Zheng to the end did not know who his killers were.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng never knew who his killers were.

sentences.zh: 時年三十四。

translations.literal: He was thirty-four years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was thirty-four years old.

sentences.zh: 有遺腹子政道，與蕭後同入突厥，處羅可汗號為隋王，中國人沒入北蕃者，悉配之以為部落，以定襄城處之。
