translations.literal: He had a posthumous son Zhengdao, who entered the Turks together with Empress Xiao; Quluo Khan styled him Prince of Sui; Chinese taken captive in the northern barbarian lands were all assigned to him as a tribe, and they were settled at Dingxiang city.
translations.idiomatic: He had a posthumous son Zhengdao, who entered the Turks together with Empress Xiao; Quluo Khan styled him Prince of Sui; Chinese taken captive in the northern lands were all assigned to him as a tribe and settled at Dingxiang.

sentences.zh: 及突厥滅，歸於大唐，授員外散騎侍郎。

translations.literal: When the Turks were destroyed he returned to Great Tang and was appointed Vice Director of the Attendant Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks were destroyed he returned to the Tang and was appointed Vice Director of the Attendant Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 趙王趙王杲，小字季子。

translations.literal: Prince of Zhao Gao, childhood name Jizi—the text repeats the title—
translations.idiomatic: Prince Gao of Zhao, whose childhood name was Jizi,

sentences.zh: 年七歲，以封趙王。

translations.literal: at the age of seven was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
translations.idiomatic: was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao at the age of seven.

sentences.zh: 尋授光祿大夫，拜河南尹。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made Intendant of Henan.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and made Intendant of Henan.

sentences.zh: 從幸淮南，詔行江都太守事。

translations.literal: He followed the emperor to Huainan and was ordered to act as Administrator of Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the emperor to Huainan and was ordered to act as Administrator of Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 杲聰令，美容儀，帝有所制詞賦，杲多能誦之。

translations.literal: Gao was clever and bright, handsome in bearing; whenever the emperor composed lyrics or rhapsodies, Gao could often recite them.
translations.idiomatic: Gao was clever and bright, handsome in bearing; whenever the emperor composed lyrics or rhapsodies, Gao could often recite them from memory.

sentences.zh: 性至孝，常見帝風動不進膳，杲亦終日不食。

translations.literal: By nature he was utterly filial; whenever he saw the emperor troubled by wind and refusing food, Gao also would not eat all day.
translations.idiomatic: By nature he was utterly filial; whenever he saw the emperor unwell and refusing food, Gao also would not eat all day.

sentences.zh: 又蕭後當灸，杲先請試炷，後不許之，杲泣請曰：「後所服藥，皆蒙嘗之。

translations.literal: Moreover when Empress Xiao was to undergo moxibustion, Gao first begged to test the cautery; the empress would not allow it; Gao wept and pleaded: "All the medicines the empress takes, I have tasted for her.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover when Empress Xiao was to undergo moxibustion, Gao first begged to test the cautery himself; the empress refused; Gao wept and pleaded, "All the medicines the empress takes, I have tasted for her.

sentences.zh: 今灸，願聽嘗炷。

translations.literal: Now for moxibustion, I beg to be allowed to taste the cautery first."
translations.idiomatic: Now for moxibustion, I beg to be allowed to test the cautery first."

sentences.zh: 」悲咽不已。

translations.literal: " He sobbed without cease.
translations.idiomatic: " He sobbed without cease.

sentences.zh: 後竟為其停灸，由是尤愛之。

translations.literal: The empress in the end suspended the moxibustion for his sake, and because of this loved him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: The empress in the end suspended the moxibustion for his sake, and because of this loved him all the more.

sentences.zh: 後遇化及反，杲在帝側，號慟不已。

translations.literal: Later when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the emperor's side, crying and wailing without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Later when Huaji rebelled, Gao was at the emperor's side, crying and wailing without cease.

sentences.zh: 裴虔通使賊斬之於帝前，血湔禦服。

translations.literal: Pei Qiantong had the rebels behead him before the emperor; blood splashed the imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Qiantong had the rebels behead him before the emperor; blood splashed the imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 時年十二。

translations.literal: He was twelve years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was twelve years old.

sentences.zh: 【論】史臣曰：元德太子雅性謹重，有君人之量，降年不永，哀哉！

translations.literal: [Commentary] The historiographer says: The Yuande Heir Apparent by nature was refined and grave, with the measure of a ruler; his years were cut short—how mournful!
translations.idiomatic: [Commentary] The historiographer says: The Yuande Heir Apparent was refined and grave by nature, with the measure of a ruler; his years were cut short—how mournful!

sentences.zh: 齊王敏慧可稱，志不及遠，頗懷驕僭，故煬帝疏而忌之。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qi was clever and admirable, but his aims did not reach far; he rather harbored arrogance and presumption, and so Emperor Yang kept him at a distance and was wary of him.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zheng of Qi was clever and admirable, but his aims did not reach far; he rather harbored arrogance and presumption, and so Emperor Yang kept him at a distance and was wary of him.

sentences.zh: 心無父子之親，貌展君臣之敬，身非積善，國有餘殃。

translations.literal: In heart he had no bond of father and son; in appearance he displayed the respect of subject and ruler; his person had not accumulated goodness, and the state bore remaining calamity.
translations.idiomatic: In heart he had no bond of father and son; in appearance he displayed the respect of subject and ruler; his person had not accumulated goodness, and the state bore the calamity that followed.

sentences.zh: 至令趙及燕、越皆不得其死，悲夫！

translations.literal: So that even Zhao and Yan and Yue all failed to meet natural deaths—how lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: So that even the princes of Zhao, Yan, and Yue all failed to meet natural deaths—how lamentable!
